subject: Commercial amendment for Azure Private Plan — data processing clause & billing cadence
messages:
From: Katie Brown <katie.brown@contoso.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Contoso Procurement <procurement@contoso.com>, Azure ISV Team <azureisv@microsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 17:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Contoso redlines for Azure Private Plan DPA + billing cadence

Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached are Contoso's redlines to the DPA and a short note on preferred billing cadence. High level:

- Data residency & subprocessors: we need a clearer commitment that logs and customer data for EU tenants remain in EU regions for the retention period.
- Audit rights: contoso legal requests a 30-day notice window before any subprocessor changes.
- Billing cadence: we prefer quarterly invoicing (net-30) for the first 12 months instead of monthly to align with our vendor payment cycles.

I've attached the PDF with tracked changes (Contoso_Redlines_DPA_20261122.pdf) and the quote spreadsheet (Azure_PrivatePlan_Quote_20261120.xlsx). Can you confirm whether these are acceptable or where Redwood needs to escalate?

Best,
Katie Brown
Head of Procurement, Contoso

Subject: Re: Contoso redlines for Azure Private Plan DPA + billing cadence

Hi Katie — thank you for the clear redlines. Appreciate the level of detail. Quick notes from our side:

- Data residency: we can commit that customer production data and application logs for EU tenants will be served and stored in EU regions. Our retention/export logs may be replicated to a central control plane in the US for operational telemetry; we can add contractual language limiting that telemetry to metadata only and excluding PII.

- Subprocessor notice: 30-day notice is reasonable for major subprocessor changes. For critical emergency changes (e.g., CVE mitigations), we'd ask for a shorter communication path but can include an escalation clause to notify customers as soon as practical.

- Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing is not our default for Private plans, but we can propose a 3-month invoice cadence for the first year with an annual reconciliation. I will need a finance point to confirm the net terms.

Looping in Marissa (legal) and Naomi (finance) to validate the DPA language and billing options.

Next step: Marissa/Naomi — can you review the attached redlines and indicate which items require legal escalation vs. standard Commercial Ops edits? Also marking this as DEAL-18942-AZ in HubSpot.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping, David. I've reviewed Contoso's redlines quickly and flagged the following items that will need legal review and possible executive sign-off: 

1) Data residency guarantee: we can commit to region-bound storage for customer data, but we must be explicit about the control plane/telemetry exceptions. Proposed wording: "Customer Data (as defined) will be stored and processed within the EU for EU tenants; Redwood will not export Customer Data containing PII to other regions for operational use. Telemetry and aggregated metrics, devoid of PII, may be processed outside the EU for monitoring and service improvements."

2) Audit & access: Contoso requires a 30-day notice for subprocessor changes. We can accept this with the caveat that emergency changes will follow an "expedited notification" path and post-implementation disclosure for critical security patches.

3) Indemnity caps and liability language: Contoso added expanded carve-outs — we should push back to maintain our standard liability cap; if Contoso insists on higher exposure, we will need executive approval.

4) Billing cadence: finance input required. Naomi, are quarterly invoices with net-30 reconciliations workable from Redwood's perspective? If not, propose alternative approach and I'll draft language that minimizes cashflow risk.

I've attached a quick redline summary (internal memo) and highlighted the highest-risk clauses. If Contoso will accept our telemetry/PII carveout and standard liability cap, we can proceed without legal escalation. Otherwise, I recommend a short exec approval (CRO/GC).

Marissa
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:45:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Contoso redlines for Azure Private Plan DPA + billing cadence

Marissa/David — thanks for the quick review. A couple of clarifications from our side to keep the discussion moving: 

- Telemetry: Contoso will accept a telemetry carveout if Redwood provides a short public spec on what telemetry is collected and a commitment that no PII will be included. Can you produce that spec?
- Emergency subprocessor changes: the expedited notification path you mentioned sounds reasonable; Contoso asks that changes be logged and visible via a customer portal or an email distribution list.
- Liability: Contoso legal is open to Redwood's standard cap if Redwood adds a mutual breach clause (both parties responsible for their respective failures).

Finally, on billing: Contoso will agree to monthly billing for the first 6 months if Redwood offers 45-day payment terms (net-45) for those invoices; otherwise we will need quarterly invoicing. Can your finance team confirm?

Best,
Procurement Team
Contoso

Quick executive note — adding my perspective as head of Strategic Accounts. Contoso is a reference target in EMEA and this deal unlocks a marketplace co-sell path with Microsoft. Two asks before I sign off: 

1) If legal and finance can agree to the telemetry spec (explicit list + confirmation of no PII) and an expedited-notice subprocessor clause, I authorize pushing the standard liability cap with a mutual-breach clause.

2) For billing, finance should accept net-45 for the first 6 months; if that's a blocker we should accept quarterly invoicing but request an upfront 25% deposit on activation. Naomi — can you confirm which option minimizes revenue risk while keeping the Contoso procurement timeline?

If we can close with those two items, I'll approve the executive amendment and instruct Legal to prepare the final signature packet (DocuSign link to follow).

Thanks — I'll be available for a short call if the team wants to sync.
